title: Written Thesis Rubric
description: For short-form written capstones and the final 1500-word thesis. The point is defensibility, not polish.

levels.descriptor: No identifiable claim. Reader cannot summarize the position in one sentence.
Claim is present but vague, hedged into meaninglessness, or buried.
Claim is stated plainly and a reader could repeat it back accurately.
Claim is sharp, falsifiable, and the writer signals exactly how confident they are.
Assertions without support. Conclusions do not follow from premises.
Some reasoning, but key steps are skipped or rest on undefended assumptions.
The argument follows. A skeptical reader can trace each step.
The argument follows AND the writer flags its weakest link before a critic has to.
No counter-argument considered. Or only a strawman version.
A counter-argument appears but is dismissed without being taken seriously.
A real counter-argument is engaged and answered.
The strongest version of the counter-argument is steel-manned, and the response either holds or the writer updates.
Generic, hedged, or AI-flavored prose. Reader cannot tell who wrote it or why they care.
Some personal stake visible but mostly safe and recycled.
Clear voice. The writer is in the room.
Clear voice AND visible intellectual honesty about uncertainty, change of mind, or what would change the writer's view.
